item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: its Files.Upload uses the established multipart helper and delegates to FilesService.Add, preserving existing option, request, response, and error behavior. B directly contradicts two explicit constraints by duplicating Add and refactoring global raw/retry behavior.","reasons":["A calls multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content) and then s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), exactly matching the required repository pattern and delegation path.","A’s retry test uses a non-seekable reader, directly exercising the requirement that Upload buffer streamed content into a replayable body.","B reimplements FilesService.Add logic inside Upload instead of routing through Add, creating duplicate request construction and response decoding machinery.","B changes RawClient.Do semantics for every io.ReadSeeker, despite the explicit instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery. Its GetBody closure also repeatedly mutates one shared seeker, which is more fragile than the established buffered-body mechanism requested by the contract."],"risks_a":["It adds an unrelated PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the requirement to add exactly the specified convenience API.","Its multipart test checks the field and filename but never reads and verifies the uploaded content.","It omits explicit tests for empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, and source-reader failures, all required by the contract."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, violating a central architectural requirement and risking future divergence in options and error semantics.","The broad RawClient.Do changes alter ownership, closing, content-length, seeking, and retry behavior for raw calls plus Files.Add/Update, all outside the authorized scope.","Its Upload retry test uses an os.File rather than a forward-only streamed reader, so the new global seeker-replay machinery can mask whether multipartbody.NewFile itself provides the required replayability path already used elsewhere in the SDK consistency contract. It also omits a source-reader failure test."]}
